note: P4365 (Pro 30:10) — do not slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you be held guilty.

dims.v: malicious tale-bearing — accusing a servant to his master, and incurring guilt
the slandering of a servant to his master — malicious tale-bearing against one who cannot easily defend himself, which recoils in a curse and guilt on the slanderer
(the guilt it brings on the slanderer)
the malicious accusation that rebounds on the one who makes it

lashan (slander/accuse) — 'do not SLANDER a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty' (30:10); malicious accusation, especially of the lowly, brings guilt on the accuser. To injure a servant with the tongue is to court a curse (cf 6:16-19).
